title.narrative: Notfallvorsorge durch verbesserte Hanglagenbewirtschaftung in den bedrohten ländlichen Gebieten der DVR Korea

description.narrative: Extreme rainfall causes a lot of damage to many parts of North Korea almost every year and adversely affects the unstable and often heavily-deforested slopes of this mountainous country. This project focuses on promoting improved and more protective hillside cultivation. The people working these fields, often pensioners and widows, do not belong (any longer) to conventional farmers cooperatives, putting them in a particularly precarious situation. They receive advice about more modern, resource-efficient cultivation methods and on how to replace firewood with energy-efficient fuels. In addition, disaster preparedness increases their resilience to shocks.
Improved sloping land cultivation methods of eight rural counties in the Provinces North-Pyongan, South-Pyongan and Kangwon improves the disaster prepardness and diversifies its food supply.

Sloping land user groups(SLUG) in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea are the principle vulnerable groups. The members of SLUG are those people who can't work in cooperative farms or other institutions. They may be, for example, retired or widowed. Experience from the previous projects show that the groups consist of a majority of women, primarily older women.
